Proposes an approach; secondary: Evaluates — SkillReducer, two-stage skill debloating (delta-debugging description compression and taxonomy-driven progressive disclosure), evaluated on 600 skills and SkillsBench against original skills and four compression baselines; preceded by an empirical study of 55,315 skills
SkillReducer (proposed; no version). Compared: original skill (A), no skill (D), LLMLingua, direct LLM compression, truncation, random sentence removal; ablation variants C1-C4

Agent skills (Anthropic skill protocol: SKILL.md with routing description and Markdown body, optional reference files, scripts out of scope). Output: compressed routing description; compressed core body (always loaded); on-demand reference modules (examples.md, templates.md, background.md, deduplicated references) annotated with 'when' clause and 3-5 topic keywords

Stage 1 (routing layer): segment description into semantic clauses -> DDMIN with simulated routing oracle (TF-IDF distractors + LLM adversarial skill) -> paraphrase/polish -> real trigger validation via Claude Code CLI with selective restore or fallback; generate missing descriptions. Stage 2 (body): classify paragraphs (core rule, background, example, template, redundant) -> type-specific compression -> cross-file deduplication -> annotate references -> Gate 1 faithfulness check -> Gate 2 task evaluation with feedback loop (promote items to core, max 2 iterations)

Automatic: tokenizer counts, assertion tests (52.3% of Gate 2 evaluations), LLM judge Qwen3.5 (47.7%; validated vs deterministic verifier, kappa=0.939 on 1,646 tasks), Claude Code CLI stream events for routing; tasks and rubrics LLM-generated

Authors' stated success criterion (p. 4, 7-8): an optimized skill must keep routing equivalence (selected for the same queries) and functional retention (same task performance as the original: a skill passes Gate 2 when scoreC >= scoreA, retention = 1.0, on every task), with Cost(s') much lower than Cost(s). The criterion applies to compressed configurations; No skill (D, lower bound) and Original skill (A, reference) get 'no criterion stated by the authors'. Verdicts below apply the authors' criterion only (no extractor threshold). Main study (600 skills, 5 tasks each, authors' harness with read_file tool + Qwen3.5; Table III): (1) No skill (D): 0.684; quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors. (2) Original skill (A): 0.722; quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors. (3) SkillReducer (C): 0.742; 86.0% of skills meet scoreC >= scoreA (CI 83.1-88.7), C>A 25.3%, C<A 14.0%, p=0.002, d=0.107; body -39.0%, description -48.0%, end-to-end input -26.8%; one-time compression about 14-18 USD for 600 skills; quality: partly (criterion met by 86.0% of skills, not all); cost: works (cost well below the original). Non-ceiling subset (481): D 0.606, A 0.653, C 0.678, pass 82.5%. SkillsBench (87 tasks; harness and model not stated): D 86/87 and A 87/87 (no criterion stated by the authors; A body 359K tokens); C 87/87, zero regression, body 84K tokens, 84 of 87 compressed (quality: works; cost: works). Baselines (50 skills, same token budget as C, authors' harness + Qwen3.5; Table IV), score / mean retention: A 0.921 (no criterion stated by the authors); C 0.909 / 0.949; LLMLingua 0.767 / 0.820; LLM direct compression 0.866 / 0.918; truncation 0.791 / 0.845; random sentence removal 0.694 / 0.750; each compressed method: quality: partly (mean retention below 1.0, so the criterion is not met on every task); cost: works (same reduced budget as C). Ablation (50 skills x 5 tasks; Table VI; per-variant tokens not reported), score / retention: D 0.559 / 0.596 and A 0.939 / 1.000 (no criterion stated by the authors); full C 0.926 / 0.987 (partly); C1 description only 0.925 / 0.985 (partly); C2 body compression without classification 0.882 / 0.940 (partly); C3 reference deduplication only 0.944 / 1.000 (works); C4 compress all without classification 0.863 / 0.919 (partly); cost: not reported for the variants. Cross-model (30 skills x 5 tasks, compressor DeepSeek-V3, authors' harness + model; Table VIII), scoreA / scoreC / retention: GLM-5 0.926 / 0.962 / 0.986; DeepSeek-V3 0.936 / 0.963 / 0.978; Qwen3-max 0.931 / 0.930 / 0.955; GPT-OSS-120B (flat injection, no tool calling) 0.951 / 0.958 / 0.982; Qwen2.5-7B 0.920 / 0.893 / 0.939; C quality: partly for every model (retention below 1.0); cost: not reported per model. Cross-compressor (same 30 skills, evaluator fixed but not named; only retention reported): compressor DeepSeek-V3 0.896, Qwen3-max 0.897, Qwen2.5-7B 0.874 (quality: partly; cost: not reported). Cross-framework (OpenCode v1.2.27 + DeepSeek-V3, 30 skills x 3 tasks): A 0.751 (no criterion stated by the authors); C 0.764, retention 0.944 (quality: partly; cost: not reported). Routing (Claude Code CLI, model not stated; Table V): compressed descriptions preserve routing for 536/536 non-obsolete skills (42.0% direct, 40.8% after selective restore, 6.5% fallback to original), 65% mean description compression among passed (quality: works; cost: works)

Paired design per skill: conditions D (no skill), A (original), C (compressed, references via read_file, max 6 tool calls). Baselines at equal token budget. Held constant: tasks, evaluator model (Qwen3.5, separate API key from compressor DeepSeek-V3), temperature 0 for classification. Acceptance tests: assertion-based scripts for code tasks, LLM-judge rubrics, SkillsBench pytest verifiers. Repetitions: one run per task (not stated otherwise); bootstrap CIs. Human intervention: none

C > A on average (0.742 vs 0.722, Wilcoxon p=0.002, d=0.107, small); holds without ceiling cases (p=0.010); text says gain larger for long official skills (+11.8 pp vs +1.1 pp community), but Table III gives Official 0.743 -> 0.831 (+8.8 pp). SkillReducer beats all four compression baselines (one-sided sign tests, p<=0.003). Taxonomy classification key (C4 retention 0.919, -6.8 pp). Transfers to 5 models (mean retention 0.965) and OpenCode (0.944). Of 84 regressions, ~33% true compression failures (4.7% of skills). End-to-end input savings 26.8% (best case)

Distinguished SkillReducer from baselines and ablations; SkillsBench did not distinguish (ceiling: D 86/87). Repeatable: single runs, bootstrap CIs and paired tests. Limitations stated: Gate 2 is both optimization signal and evaluation criterion (optimization-to-criterion); LLM randomness; only Anthropic skill protocol; five models from four families; Wild study without Gate 2

Generalization to other platforms (Cursor, Windsurf) and model families (Llama) untested; Wild sample lacks task evaluation; example-as-specification failure mode (implicit rules in examples); skill obsolescence (10.7%) motivates adaptive skill lifecycle management

Inconsistencies: feedback loop recovery reported as 31/38 = 81.6% (p. 9) but 27/38 = 71.1% in Appendix E (p. 13); official-skill gain +11.8 pp in text vs +8.8 pp from Table III (0.743 -> 0.831); end-to-end savings given as 26.8% (best case), 43.2% and 57.4% (theoretical) in different places, and Appendix E calls 26.8%-43.2% 'our empirical measurement' although 43.2% is derived; cross-compressor retention for DeepSeek-V3 is 0.896 while Table VIII (same compressor, 30 skills) gives 0.965 mean and no evaluator below 0.939, with the fixed evaluator not named; SkillsBench body reduction given as 75.0% mean per task in the text, -74.1% in Figure 4, while 359K -> 84K is 76.6% in aggregate (may be different aggregations). Figure 4 label reads 'SkillsBench (17 tasks)' vs 84/87 in text (pdftotext; check figure). Tables III, IV, VI, VIII rebuilt from pdftotext column order; Table VII (sensitivity) jumbled, values not used. Agent harness for main evaluation is the authors' own pipeline with Qwen3.5; Claude Code CLI only for routing validation. Tool to be released upon acceptance (no link). No pre-registration.
